objective: Choose the safest highest-value bounded next checkpoint for a newly created fork with no durable Steward context.

candidates.title: Bounded YAML authoring support
candidates.summary: Implement a small first slice of upstream issue #16, starting at CLI document/operation input.
candidates.rationale: High agent-experience value and existing JSON validators provide a clear normalization boundary.
benefits: Improves agent authoring ergonomics without changing the canonical document model.
costs: Requires a safe YAML parser/dependency and synchronized CLI/MCP contract decisions.
technical_risks: Parser safety, anchors/tags policy, lockfile changes, and cross-surface parity need executable verification.
product_risks: A CLI-only slice could temporarily diverge from the repository rule that public contracts stay synchronized.
unknowns: Preferred MCP envelope/field design and YAML subset are not yet accepted product decisions.
assumptions: Upstream issue #16 remains a proposal, not fork-specific accepted scope.
research_questions: What smallest YAML boundary preserves parity without creating a second document model?

candidates.title: Complete offline source handoff export
candidates.summary: Begin phase one of upstream issue #17 around the existing React/Vite source ZIP.
candidates.rationale: Very high user value because it turns designs into portable editable projects.
benefits: Directly supports handoff to developers and coding agents.
costs: Touches export service, tokens, assets, manifest, docs and multiple public surfaces.
technical_risks: Broad scope and fidelity/security requirements need isolated runtime tests unavailable in this session.
product_risks: Likely collision with ongoing upstream evolution and a large acceptance surface.
unknowns: Exact current React export ownership and a safe minimum phase require deeper direct-checkout inspection.
assumptions: Upstream issue #17 is evidence of a possible direction, not authorization.
research_questions: What is the smallest complete offline handoff slice that can be proven in isolation?

candidates.title: Remote Steward continuity bootstrap
candidates.summary: Make no product change; first establish truthful durable repository context on a feature branch.
candidates.rationale: The fork is new, has no .repo-steward/, no fork-specific branch/PR history, and this session cannot run local product verification. Durable continuity removes ambiguity without creating unverified product code.
benefits: Creates a safe continuity baseline for fresh agents.
Avoids product regression claims without runtime evidence.
Does not collide with upstream PR #37.
costs: Defers visible product functionality by one checkpoint.
technical_risks: Canonical Repo Steward content digest still needs a future direct checkout.
product_risks: Minimal; product behavior is intentionally unchanged.
unknowns: Which product candidate should follow after local reconciliation.
assumptions: The active user request authorizes selecting and implementing one bounded checkpoint while withholding merge/deploy/release authority.
research_questions: What durable artifacts can be truthfully persisted without fabricating a direct-checkout snapshot?

candidates.title: Stop after assessment
candidates.summary: Leave the fork untouched and report candidate directions only.
candidates.rationale: Would avoid all mutation, but fails to create the repository-owned durable continuity explicitly requested by the mission.
candidates.rejection_reason: The active mission authorizes a bounded implementation and specifically requires durable repository-owned handoff when safe.
costs: A fresh agent would still have no durable context.

limitations: Upstream issues and PRs are signals, not accepted fork decisions.
No local checkout/runtime verification is available in this session.
